context_requirements: Expression of one or more cytochrome P450 enzymes (especially CYP3A4/5, CYP2C9/19, CYP1B1) that the drug can inhibit
An intact endogenous CYP-dependent pathway whose flux changes when the enzyme is inhibited
For hepatocyte-like lines, active xenobiotic and sterol regulatory programs
falsifiers: No change in any CYP or NR3C1/NR3C2 transcript at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
A clear, strong and reproducible transcriptional signature at 6 h in all nine lines, which would suggest a non-specific cytotoxic or stress response rather than CYP inhibition
No dose-dependent or time-dependent changes in the expected direction in HEPG2, the line with the most complete CYP repertoire

evidence.supports: A cytochrome P450 inhibitor (uniconazole) can block a specific CYP-dependent biosynthetic pathway, showing that CYP inhibition can produce transcriptional consequences
The CYP inhibitor SKF-525A blocks autophagic flux in primary hepatocytes, indicating that some CYP inhibitors can perturb lysosomal/autophagic programs
Fluconazole inhibits CYP450 gene expression in vivo, supporting the possibility of transcriptional feedback on CYP genes
Itraconazole is a potent CYP3A inhibitor, confirming CYP3A as a target of azole-class CYP inhibitors
Fluconazole, used as a cytochrome P450 inhibitor, modulates a CYP-dependent lipid mediator pathway in vascular cells
